title: Adulis at its height
description: The Red Sea port of Adulis, later the gateway of the kingdom of Aksum, already handles the trade of the African interior.

title: Ottomans take Massawa
description: Ottoman forces seize Massawa and the coast, which their local deputies hold, off and on, for three centuries.

title: Assab Bay purchased
description: The Rubattino shipping company buys the bay of Assab for a coaling station, the first Italian foothold on this coast.

title: Italians occupy Massawa
description: Italian troops land at Massawa with British approval, the start of Italy's colonial venture on the Red Sea.

title: Battle of Dogali
description: Ethiopian troops under Ras Alula wipe out an Italian column, halting the Italian advance inland for years.

title: Italian Eritrea proclaimed
description: Italy formally creates the colony of Eritrea, giving the country its name and its modern borders.

title: Battle of Keren
description: After a hard eight-week battle British-led forces break the Italian defence of Keren, deciding the fight for Eritrea.

title: British Military Administration
description: Britain takes over the running of Eritrea and administers it until the United Nations settles its future.

title: UN federation resolution
description: The UN General Assembly decides that Eritrea will be joined to Ethiopia as an autonomous unit in a federation.

title: Federation takes effect
description: Eritrea's new elected assembly takes office and the federation with Ethiopia comes into force.

title: Armed struggle begins
description: Hamid Idris Awate and a handful of fighters open the Eritrean war of independence, which will run for thirty years.

title: Battle of Afabet
description: The EPLF destroys Ethiopia's best field army in the north in one of the most important victories of the long war.

title: Massawa falls
description: In Operation Fenkil the EPLF takes Massawa, cutting the Ethiopian army's supply line into Eritrea.

title: EPLF takes Asmara
description: EPLF forces enter Asmara, ending Ethiopian rule and beginning an administration that leads to independence two years later.

title: Nakfa introduced
description: Eritrea stops using the Ethiopian birr and issues its own currency, the nakfa.

title: G-15 crackdown
description: The government jails eleven senior critics known as the G-15 and shuts the private press, closing off political debate ever since.

title: Border ruling
description: A boundary commission at The Hague decides the disputed frontier, including the flashpoint village of Badme, but Ethiopia does not withdraw.

title: UN sanctions
description: The Security Council imposes an arms embargo and targeted sanctions over Eritrea's support for armed groups in Somalia and its quarrel with Djibouti.

title: Forto mutiny
description: Soldiers briefly occupy the information ministry at Forto demanding change, the closest thing to a public challenge to the government in years.
